context: equipment-fit-out led · floor flatness & clean utilities gate a fast, repeatable line install

brief.intro: A light or discrete manufacturing plant assembles or packages products on production lines built from off-the-shelf and semi-custom machines, conveyors and AGVs, rather than heavy custom process equipment. Unlike a heavy industrial factory, the machines are lighter and mostly bolt to a flat floor instead of needing isolated foundations, so the building shell can go up fast and the real programme driver becomes a flat, tolerance-checked floor slab and clean utilities ready in time for the machine vendors. HVAC is more than comfort cooling here — in pharma, food or electronics variants it becomes environmental control or full cleanroom qualification, and that qualification chain can dominate the back end of the schedule. The line itself is commissioned as a system: machines are proven individually (SAT), then integrated with conveyors/AGVs, then dry-run without product, before a loaded production ramp-up. Because machine installation often follows shortly after building handover, planners need to coordinate the building contractor's finish date directly with the machine vendors' install windows.

scope.name: Structure & shell
scope.desc: Frame, envelope and roofing — weather-tight fast so floor and fit-out can start.

scope.name: Floor & floor flatness
scope.desc: Power-floated production slab finished to a flatness (F-number) tolerance for AGVs and machine alignment.

scope.name: Utilities to point of use
scope.desc: Electrical power, compressed air, process water, exhaust — terminated at each machine location.

scope.name: HVAC & environmental control
scope.desc: Comfort/process HVAC, or cleanroom-grade filtration and pressure cascades where applicable.

scope.name: Machines & production lines
scope.desc: Procurement, delivery, set and align of packaged/skid production equipment.

scope.name: Material handling
scope.desc: Conveyors, AGVs and palletisers linking stations into a line.

scope.name: Controls & data
scope.desc: PLC/SCADA field devices and MES/data integration.

scope.name: Testing & commissioning
scope.desc: Machine SAT, line integration, dry run, then loaded production ramp.

glossary.plain: Site Acceptance Test — proving a machine works correctly after it is installed.
automated guided vehicle — a driverless cart that moves parts or material between stations.
how flat and level the floor is, checked against a number so AGVs and machines run true.
the staged proof — Installation, Operational, Performance Qualification — that a controlled space works and stays in spec.
running the line without real product to prove the mechanics before committing material.
the software layer that tracks production and talks to the machine controllers (PLCs).
HVAC held to tighter temperature, humidity or particulate limits than ordinary comfort cooling.

must_get_right: Floor flatness and utility point-of-use readiness are gating conditions for machine install — verify them before, not after, vendors mobilise.
Coordinate building handover directly with the machine vendors' installation windows; a late shell pushes the whole line.
If the process needs cleanroom or tight environmental control, plan the IQ/OQ/PQ qualification chain as its own schedule phase, not a punch-list item.
Commission line-by-line — SAT each machine, then integrate, then dry-run — before any loaded ramp-up.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structural trades run a standard 6-day week; production-equipment install and utility termination move to two shifts as machine vendors mobilise together; commissioning runs an extended calendar once machine SAT begins, aligned with vendor-technician availability.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs structure/envelope close-in → production-floor flatness verification → utilities to point of use → equipment delivery & set → machine SAT → line/cell integration → dry run → loaded ramp-up. Where the process needs cleanroom or tight environmental control, HVAC qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) runs in parallel with equipment set and must complete before the dry run.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design and machine-vendor layout drawings are frozen ahead of floor and utility rough-in; the client free-issues no equipment; a single mobilisation; utilities (grid power, water, gas where applicable) are available to the site boundary by the date assumed. Any change to these invalidates the baseline dates.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Machine-vendor technicians mobilise in a compressed window once the floor and utilities are ready, so laydown and crane/forklift access for offloading are a site constraint; floor-flatness rework, if triggered, displaces every following trade.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: floor-flatness non-conformance discovered late, machine or steel-package delivery slippage, and cleanroom/HVAC qualification failures forcing a re-test. Schedule contingency is held before line integration and before the loaded ramp-up rather than spread thinly across activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
